solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One left rolling over behind inn, got rid of, put out

indicators.note: behind places the following letters after the inn

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: rolling over turns the pair of letters for one and left backwards

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
to shed something is to get rid of it

explanation.surface: Someone tumbling backwards behind a pub, discarding things and thoroughly put out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolling over' turns IL into LI, which sits after PUB.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a book that has been issued to the public has been brought out.

clue.text: They may have 10 very good and one being nuisance endlessly

parts.note: PI, short for pious, is crossword slang for very good

indicators.note: endlessly cuts off the last letter of the word for a nuisance

parts.note: a pest is a nuisance

explanation.surface: A puzzling statement about something very good alongside a constant annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 is the answer to 10 across, TOBACCO; smokers fill these with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: smoking pipes are packed with tobacco, the answer to 10 across.

clue.text: Times for catching someone going wild — courage needed

indicators.note: for catching means the word for times holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: BY is the multiplication sign read as a word: three by four is three times four
a raver is someone who parties wildly

explanation.surface: A newspaper trying to capture a wild partygoer needs nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but is the multiplication word BY.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: courage and boldness in the face of danger are the same quality.

clue.text: Read print, tree having been destroyed?

indicators.note: destroyed letters are broken up and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Printing on paper, read once a tree has been felled to make it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to read a text or signal in a particular way is to construe its meaning.

clue.text: Like some medicine that's bad for him — too cheap

indicators.note: bad signals that the letters of the following words are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: A grumble that a remedy is wrong for a patient because it is far too cheap.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: one kind of alternative medicine uses highly diluted remedies on a like-cures-like principle.

clue.text: Little girl making a point

definitions.meaning: A girl's name, short for Dorothy
a small round mark or spot

explanation.surface: A small girl making her point.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a pet form of Dorothy, and a tiny spot.

clue.text: Signal made by British PM heading west

indicators.note: in an across clue, heading west means reading from right to left

parts.note: Sir Robert Peel was a British Prime Minister

explanation.surface: A British prime minister sends a message while travelling west.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Robert Peel founded the Metropolitan Police; 'heading west' works because this is an across entry, read right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a short electronic tone used as a signal or to mask a word.

clue.text: Confusion with black man getting murdered

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
Abel was killed by his brother Cain in Genesis

explanation.surface: Chaos surrounds a black man who is killed.
explanation.definitionFit: Allusion: the Tower of Babel story ends with a confusion of tongues, so the name means uproar.

clue.text: Racine magically penning line in ordianry language

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so one piece sits inside the other
magically transformed letters appear in a new order

explanation.surface: The French dramatist Racine, as if by magic, writing a line in plain speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'magically' rearranges RACINE to ENCAIR; 'penning' puts L inside. The clue's 'ordianry' is a misprint of ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: French for 'in clear', said of messages sent unencoded, in plain words.

clue.text: Driven to offer support to the French female and daughter

parts.note: to prop something is to support it
elle is French for she

explanation.surface: Pushed into helping a Frenchwoman and her child.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something pushed forward by a force has been moved onward.

clue.text: Some elephant ominously apppearing? It's an illusion

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An elephant looms up threateningly, but it is only a trick of the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a ghostly apparition is something seen that is not really there.

clue.text: Explorer taken aback by firm producing harmful product

indicators.note: taken aback suggests the explorer's name is turned back to front

parts.note: John Cabot was a Venetian explorer who sailed for England
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: An explorer startled by a company making something dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' reads as surprise but turns CABOT into TOBAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: smoking leaf is a well-known damaging commodity.

clue.text: Son never heartlessly making scornful comment

indicators.note: heartlessly removes the central letter of the word never

explanation.surface: A son who never says anything kind, mocking others cruelly.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a contemptuous remark or expression of disdain.

clue.text: What swinger will do in local site naughtily

indicators.note: naughtily behaving letters stray into a different order

explanation.surface: A racy hint about a swinger's behaviour at some nearby venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swinger' suggests a promiscuous person, but here it is just something that sways, like a pendulum.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: anything that swings moves to and fro.

clue.text: Birds in rubbish in bottomless box

parts.note: chaff is worthless husks, hence rubbish

indicators.note: bottomless drops the last letter, the bottom of a down entry

parts.note: a chest is a large box

explanation.surface: Birds found nesting in rubbish inside a box with no base.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: common European finches with pink breasts.

clue.text: Horse in wet coastal area

explanation.surface: A horse standing in a soggy shoreline area.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a chestnut-coloured horse, and a broad inlet of sea.

clue.text: Troubled men sob? Nay, certainly not!

indicators.note: troubled letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Upset men in tears, yet someone denies it firmly.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a phrase of emphatic refusal or denial.

clue.text: Officer briefly arranged a Daimler for transport

indicators.note: transport means carrying off or into rapture, so the letters are carried into a new order

parts.note: ARR is the short form of arranged, as on sheet music

explanation.surface: A naval officer has had a Daimler car laid on to get around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for transport' looks like the car's purpose, but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a naval flag officer ranking below a vice admiral.

clue.text: Deluded maiden is wanting good Scottish boy

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for maiden over
guid is the Scots spelling of good
Ed is a boy's name, short for Edward

explanation.surface: A deluded young woman lacks a good Scottish lad.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone acting on mistaken beliefs is misled.

clue.text: Workers in the dark have this thing as a result?

parts.note: the word thing, rearranged, results in night: so the answer read as instruction describes how thing shifts

explanation.surface: A question about what nocturnal workers end up with.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: the letters of 'thing' shift to produce the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Teams working overnight shifts labour in the hours of darkness.

clue.text: Novelist taking first prize in front of glitterati

parts.note: gold is the medal for first place

indicators.note: front of picks the opening letter of the word glitterati

explanation.surface: An author wins the top award before a celebrity crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: William Golding, author of Lord of the Flies.

clue.text: Fox sending 5 into a spin

indicators.note: sending into a spin turns the cross-referenced word round

parts.note: 5 refers to the answer to 5 down, the little girl's name

explanation.surface: A fox throws a girl into panic.
explanation.walkthrough: TOD is an old and dialect word for a fox.
explanation.definitionFit: Dialect: a fox has long been called this in Scotland and northern England.

clue.text: Town crier could have this hat, we suspect

indicators.note: suspect means the letters are doubtful and so rearranged, with ours set aside

explanation.surface: A town crier might wear a hat like this, or so we suppose.
explanation.walkthrough: TOWN CRIER's letters are the answer plus WE: 'we suspect' marks the composite.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a three-cornered hat, traditionally worn by town criers.

clue.text: Terrible man, heartless, callous, like a slug

indicators.note: terrible letters are mangled into a new arrangement
heartless removes the middle letter of the word man

explanation.surface: An awful, cruel and unfeeling man, compared to a slimy creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes A from MAN, leaving MN to join CALLOUS in the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Category: slugs belong to the soft-bodied invertebrate phylum including snails.

clue.text: Style of language in American period

parts.note: an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A way of speaking found in a particular American era.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the customary way words are used in a language.

clue.text: Unfortunate warrior in old city, one with gasp of disappointment?

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city in Mesopotamia
I is the Roman numeral one
ah is a sighing exclamation

explanation.surface: A doomed soldier in an ancient city lets out a sigh of dismay.
explanation.definitionFit: Biblical figure: the Hittite soldier King David sent to die in battle to take his wife.

clue.text: Innkeepers getting hordes?

definitions.meaning: great multitudes, as in a heavenly multitude

explanation.surface: Landlords facing crowds of customers.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: people who entertain guests, and large crowds.

clue.text: Italian blocking an entrance creates stir

indicators.note: blocking means standing in the way, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: An Italian standing in a doorway causes a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to stir a liquid is to shake or churn it.

clue.text: One that has a drum to bring attention

definitions.meaning: the organ of hearing contains the eardrum
as in to have someone's attention or lend a listening organ

explanation.surface: A drummer calling everyone to attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the organ containing a tympanum, and a willing hearing.

clue.text: Hoorid dens — time to escape

indicators.note: to escape means one letter leaves the word for dens

parts.note: dens are hiding places

explanation.surface: Awful lairs from which it is time to flee.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something ghastly and repulsive to look at.

clue.text: Keep going, say, when hugged by girl

indicators.note: hugged by means held inside the girl's name

parts.note: Sue is a girl's name
EG, for example, means say

explanation.surface: Someone told to carry on while being embraced by a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Music term: to move on without a break into the next section.

clue.text: Tiredness possibly problematical for hotel guests?

indicators.note: something problematical is in a muddle, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Fatigue may cause trouble for people staying at a hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: people staying in a hotel are its live-in occupants.
